sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 39 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Road-limit estimates from USDA NAIP captured 5 July 2020, inspected at native 0.6 m spacing and compared with 2018 and 2022 imagery. Limits follow the paved circuit beside visible paint/curb transitions, excluding grass shoulders, fence lines, gravel runoff and paddock lanes. Curved intervals follow the saved road stations between sparse observations, with extra anchors through the tighter bends. Both edges across the paddock junction at stations 676–692 join neighbouring measurements with straight segments to avoid a small kink in the mapped trace. Both edges near station 12 and isolated limits at stations 432, 474, 576, 684 and 690 interpolate across access openings or vehicle occlusion. The outer closure at the pit merge is a virtual join fitted to adjoining visible limits, not a surveyed pavement edge through the opening. The two catalogue entries share exactly the same source geometry, so this recipe is reused without fitting a second road. Original traces, timing and terrain remain unchanged. Native pixel spacing is not positional accuracy; rendered curbs remain illustrative and banking unknown.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed directly from complete, sparse image measurements on the existing trace cross-sections. All intervals interpolate between image anchors; they are not automatic detections or a continuous edge survey. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. Isolated missing pixels inside the road are not filled or used as boundary evidence. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. These borders have not been formally verified.
